title: Cursor pricing: billing basis and cost boundaries
summary: Cursor pricing: billing basis and cost boundaries. Separate the recorded base price from unverified usage and operating costs.

sections.heading: One developer on a monthly plan
paragraphs: The recorded base is not a promise of unlimited model use. Before estimating a month of work, record the models, agent intensity and on-demand billing setting. Tax and overage remain outside a simple base-price comparison.

sections.heading: A team purchase
paragraphs: Multiply only a verified per-seat price by the actual seat count. Do not substitute an individual plan when administration or team privacy controls are required.

sections.heading: No task-to-credit exchange rate
paragraphs: A request, a credit and a token are not interchangeable. ToolPilot has not measured a representative workload across these products, so this guide does not invent a shared usage conversion or promise a fixed number of completed tasks.

verdict: Start with the individual subscription, then account for usage beyond the included allowance.
bestFor: Buyers checking Cursor subscription and usage assumptions
notFor: Readers seeking a guaranteed workload total without measuring usage
migration: Trial the candidate on a branch; retain the original workflow until tests, export and billing checks pass.
